rows.name: Padlet
rows.reason: A visual collaboration service provides boards and canvases, not a reusable padding function, cryptographic library, or mechanism for deciding software dependencies.

rows.name: JavaScript padStart
rows.reason: Built-in string padding illustrates avoiding a third-party dependency for a small function when the target JavaScript runtime supports it.

rows.name: Lodash padStart
rows.reason: Narrow external-library padding example; library use allowed. Compare actual package/version/usage costs, without cheaper/safer claims. Requires matching string-padding semantics and JavaScript environment; otherwise teaching-only, not implementation recommendation.

rows.name: TweetNaCl.js
rows.reason: Focused JavaScript cryptography offers a middle implementation option, not a complete protocol. JavaScript timing/memory constraints apply; an old audit does not certify current versions.

rows.name: Go Proverbs small-copying principle
rows.reason: Small-copying heuristic favors local ownership when a helper is cheaper to understand/maintain than its dependency. It is not quantitative; copied code still requires licensing, tests and maintenance.

rows.name: Padlet
rows.reason: Padlet provides visual collaboration boards and canvases, outside utility implementation, cryptographic-library selection or dependency assessment. Exclusion concerns task scope, not an asserted price, platform or security prohibition.

rows.name: libsodium higher-level cryptographic APIs
rows.reason: Higher-level cryptography supplies a library option when obligations exceed a seemingly small function. Correct key/nonce handling and integration remain necessary; current documentation lacks cutoff freezing.

rows.name: TweetNaCl
rows.reason: TweetNaCl illustrates compact embedded cryptographic reuse. Operation, toolchain, performance and maintenance ownership remain unknown; compare the chosen version. Site retrieval failed; no current security or maintenance certification is claimed.

rows.name: OWASP C2 library-adoption and encapsulation practice
rows.reason: OWASP C2 recommends dependency inventory, updates and narrow interfaces to make maintenance/integration obligations explicit. Encapsulation guarantees neither unused-code removal nor library security.

rows.name: Lodash padStart
rows.reason: A documented padding utility is a concrete library option for the single-function tradeoff; usefulness depends on existing Lodash use and dependency overhead.

rows.name: OWASP Dependency-Check
rows.reason: Component identification and known-vulnerability reporting support the continuing monitoring cost of a library decision. Coverage and component matching vary; absence of findings does not demonstrate safety.

rows.name: GitLab dependency evaluation process
rows.reason: GitLab's qualitative dependency checklist compares implementation effort, maintenance, cryptographic complexity and transitive dependencies. Availability of the live page at the cutoff was not established.

rows.name: Own a bounded utility locally — Go Proverbs heuristic
rows.reason: Go Proverbs offers a heuristic, not proof, for owning bounded utilities. Requires clear specification, reviewable edge cases and maintenance ownership; actual complexity is unknown. Current page is mutable.

rows.name: JavaScript padStart
rows.reason: Narrow comparison only: JavaScript padStart pads left. Unspecified function/language preclude verified replacement; match padding semantics and runtime support. No must prohibits it; different operations/unsupported runtimes remove applicability.

rows.name: Structured dependency review — Our Software Dependency Problem
rows.reason: The dependency review weighs reuse, ownership, failure and replacement costs, but was published 2019-01-23 after the question. Unknown failure costs, integration estimates and dependencies prevent a decision shortcut.

rows.name: npm 5 lockfiles and integrity checks
rows.reason: Lockfiles and verified cached package content help retain an upstream dependency while controlling installation variation. Does not assess selected code or remove update obligations; implementation is specific to npm.

rows.name: libsodium high-level APIs
rows.reason: Libsodium offers high-level cryptography; operation and runtime are unspecified. Verify operation/binding/version support before recommendation. Initialization, key/nonce discipline and failure handling remain application responsibilities.
